The `BisectionSolver` class has a `solve` method with the signature `solve(final UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)`. This method internally calls another `solve` method with just `min` and `max` as arguments, leading to a `NullPointerException` because the member variable `UnivariateRealSolverImpl.f` is null. To fix this issue, the `solve` method with the signature `solve(final UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max)` should be called instead.

Next, I will provide a step-by-step diagnosis of how the bug occurred.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `BisectionSolverTest.testMath369` sets up a `SinFunction` and a `BisectionSolver`, then calls `solver.solve(f, 3.0, 3.2, 3.1)` expecting the result to be `Math.PI`. However, the `BisectionSolver.solve` method with signature `solve(final UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)` internally calls another `solve` method with only `min` and `max` as arguments, leading to a `NullPointerException` because the member variable `UnivariateRealSolverImpl.f` is null. This results in the test failure. The correct method to call would be `solve(final UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max)` instead of the current call with `initial` argument.

The issue can be fixed by updating the test to call the correct `solve` method without the `initial` argument.

The root cause of the issue is the incorrect internal method call within `BisectionSolver`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
